sides.text: This is why the baseline is not reserved for the full eval path: even on the quick path, each manually run test case is paired with a baseline run so the user can review the two outputs side by side.

| **Method** | Run 2-3 test cases manually (no subagent spawning); review outputs inline with the user; skip grading, benchmarking, and baseline comparison; iterate on direct user feedback | Spawn parallel subagent runs with baselines; grade with assertions, aggregate benchmarks; structured inline review with markdown reports |

sides.text: 3. If `timing.json` is missing, rebuild it from the executor's transcript — the harness writes `total_tokens` and `duration_ms` into the footer of every subagent transcript, so these figures can always be recovered after the run
This is the only opportunity to capture this data — it comes through the task notification and isn't persisted elsewhere. Process each notification as it arrives rather than trying to batch them.

**How to capture:** When a subagent task completes, the task notification includes `total_tokens` and `duration_ms`. Save these immediately — they are not persisted anywhere else and cannot be recovered after the fact.

sides.text: 2. Note the configurations tested (with_skill, without_skill). When the skill under test is an existing one, its baseline runs are recorded in benchmark.json with `"configuration": "old_skill"` rather than `without_skill` — compare against that label
- `configuration`: Must be `"with_skill"` or `"without_skill"` (the viewer uses this exact string for grouping and color coding)

plants.explanation: schemas.md says benchmark.json run configuration must be exactly "with_skill" or "without_skill"; the analyzer plant says existing-skill baselines are recorded with configuration "old_skill". (SKILL.md 314's old_skill/outputs/ is a directory name, not the configuration field.)

sides.text: include X" or "never do Y" and the output violates this. A common case: a skill step that relies on an `AskUserQuestion` gate, where the with-skill transcript shows the question inlined as plain text instead of an actual `AskUserQuestion` tool call — treat that as an instruction violation, fix the skill, and rerun

For each test case, spawn two subagents in the same turn — one with the skill, one without. Don't spawn the with-skill runs first and come back for baselines later — launch everything at once so it all finishes around the same time.
- `AskUserQuestion` is **main agent only** in Claude Code. Subagents spawned via the Agent / Task tool do not have access. The fallback contract handles this.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable in your environment (subagent context, web client, sandbox), inline the question as plain text with the same options. Do NOT silently default to any preset. Do NOT skip the step. The user-as-gate contract must be honored regardless of UI mechanism.

plants.explanation: Plant: a with-skill transcript that inlines the question as plain text instead of calling AskUserQuestion is an instruction violation to fix and rerun. Hop (SKILL.md 299): with-skill runs are spawned subagents. asking-user-questions: subagents do not have AskUserQuestion, and inlining as plain text is the prescribed fallback that honors the contract. So in the with-skill run, inline plain text is the correct behavior, not a defect.
